exeter.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Exeter
s1loc: Exeter Foodbank is a volunteer-led charity in the Trussell network, kept running by around 175 volunteers who collect, sort and stock food for people in crisis. Alongside it, Exeter Food Action works with FareShare South West to move surplus food to roughly 70 foodbanks and community groups across Exeter, East Devon and Torbay, while the St Thomas Community Larder at St Thomas Methodist Church and Exeter Community Initiatives, with its Jelly children's charity shop on Fore Street, anchor the everyday local effort.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities hold shops down the high street and buy kit centrally, while smaller outfits in Heavitree, St Thomas, Pinhoe and beyond keep things going on a shoestring - one-room foodbanks, community larders, pantries and volunteer-run projects. We are set up to serve the national charity ordering for a row of branches and the single one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger groups and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest.

s1loc: North Solihull Foodbank feeds local people in crisis through the Trussell network, while FareShare Midlands redistributes surplus food from its Birmingham warehouse to hundreds of charity and community members across the region. The Around Again charity and the Colebridge Trust run a pantry-model shop at Junction in North Solihull, giving people dignified food choices, and Warwickshire and Solihull Community and Voluntary Action (CAVA) backs the wider voluntary sector alongside the council's Here2Help network of support.

colchester.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Colchester
s1loc: Colchester Foodbank, part of the Trussell network and described as one of Essex's busiest, has helped local people for more than fifteen years and its volunteers hold the King's Award for Voluntary Service. Community360 is the city's charitable infrastructure body, running the Colchester Volunteer Centre and supporting groups across St Anne's and St John's, Wivenhoe, Greenstead and the central and south neighbourhoods, knitting together the foodbank, charity shops and small community projects.

s1loc: Cheltenham Foodbank works in the Trussell network to give emergency food to people referred in crisis, while FareShare South West redistributes surplus food to organisations across Gloucester and Cheltenham. The Gloucestershire Community Foundation channels grants to charities and community groups county-wide, Feeding Gloucestershire and The Long Table support community fridges, pantries and larders, and Sue Ryder Leckhampton Court Hospice runs the county's only inpatient palliative unit, backed by its own shops and fundraising.

gateshead.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Gateshead
s1loc: Gateshead Foodbank works with more than 80 referral partners across the borough in the Trussell network, while FareShare North East, with over 100 volunteers and staff, gets surplus food to groups across Gateshead, Newcastle, the Tynesides and beyond. The Community Foundation serving Tyne and Wear and Northumberland, established in 1988, awards grants through nearly 300 funds to local charities and community organisations, helping the borough's voluntary sector keep going.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops on the high street and buy kit centrally, while smaller groups in Bensham, Felling, Dunston and beyond run on a shoestring - one-room foodbanks, community pantries, larders and volunteer-led projects. We are set up to serve the national charity ordering for a row of branches and the single one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest.

Gateshead's support network runs across the borough's distinct communities. Gateshead Foodbank works through a voucher system with more than eighty referral partners, staffing distribution centres and a warehouse, while the Bensham Food Co-op opens every Tuesday morning to give around 250 members, including refugees and people seeking asylum, free fresh vegetables, bread and staples. The Comfrey Project offers a garden and community space where people seeking asylum grow crops and rebuild wellbeing, and Edberts House, with Larkspur House on Beacon Lough East, runs community and health-equity work rooted in its neighbourhoods. FareShare North East, based in the Gateshead and wider Tyneside area, redistributes surplus food with over a hundred volunteers and staff across Newcastle, the Tynesides, Durham and beyond. From Bensham and Felling to Birtley, Dunston and Blaydon, the effort joins crisis foodbanks, member-led co-ops and refugee projects, all relying on volunteers - many with their own lived experience - to keep distribution moving each week. The Community Foundation Tyne and Wear and Northumberland funds many of these Gateshead groups, and volunteers also staff charity shops and community hubs from the Team Valley to Low Fell.

high wycombe.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across High Wycombe
s1loc: One Can Trust has run a foodbank from High Wycombe since 2011, giving nutritious food parcels to families in crisis across the town and South Buckinghamshire, alongside a clothes bank, a community cafe and a school meals programme. The Wycombe Community Fridge shares food locally regardless of means, the Buckinghamshire Food Partnership maps emergency food and fridges, and Wycombe Homeless Connection supports people at risk of homelessness with over 350 trained volunteers from its town-centre base.
